newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees second postponement of Yauricocha sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees second postponement of Yauricocha sale.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Thursday it was considering postponing for the second time the auction of its polymetallic mine Yauricocha due to a lack of interested bidders.

Centromin "has obtained approval from (the government) to carry out a new auction with new conditions but we are studying suspending the sale again," the government's privatization chief, Jorge Gonzales Izquierdo, told Congress.
"So far we have not detected interest from bidders. We are now thinking of selling it as a prospect instead of as an operating unit."

After an attempt to auction the asset failed to draw bidders in September, state miner Centromin - reponsible for the sale - lowered the minimum price bid to try to attract companies for a December sale.
Centromin set a minimum bid price of $8 million and hoped to receive offers for the unit on December 2.

Yauricocha, which lies 220 miles (350 km) southeast of Lima, currently produces 30,000 tonnes of mineral per month and has proven and probable reserves of 2.8 million tonnes and potential reserves of six million tonnes.
Yauricocha's auction forms part of the ongoing piecemeal privatization of Centromin, whose most important asset, the La Oroya metallurgical complex, is set to be sold in the first quarter next year.
In July, the state miner launched its sell-off with the successful sale of two of the company's major assets - the copper-rich Antamina prospect and the Quicay gold prospect .
The government also plans to sell Centromin's other six mines, a railroad network, port facilities, four hydroelectric plants and several prospects by the middle of 1997.
The Centromin sales run parallel to the ongoing privatization of assets belonging to the government's miner Minero Peru.
While Centromin's sell-off program includes operating assets as well as deposits, Minero Peru is only selling deposits.
